comparator.name: Global Law
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg's current curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, publishes 60 ECTS of mandatory study in years 1 and 2. Year 3 contains a 30-ECTS mobility window with seven approved options, followed by 30 ECTS of mandatory courses and thesis work. Because the generic bachelor does not designate one mobility option as the representative route, the comparison preserves that structured choice as a 30-ECTS component rather than selecting a minor for UCR fit. Zero-credit communication-skills and mentoring activities are noted by Tilburg but excluded from the 180 credited ECTS. The credited components total exactly 180 ECTS.

components.name: Introduction to Philosophy of Global Law
Mobility Window: one approved exchange or minor option
components.note: One 30-ECTS option is required from exchange/study abroad, Global Law and Business, Dutch Law, Law and a Sustainable Future, another Tilburg minor, a minor at another Dutch university, or a free minor.

components.name: Thesis Global Law (Final Essay)
components.note: Compulsory independent bachelor thesis concluding the programme.

It adds accounting, finance, econometrics, market research, digital strategy, organisational psychology, negotiation and international business governance. Twelve of 24 courses differ.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme captures the global and comparative legal core with explicit limits on doctrinal depth and thesis work. Official programme-specific minors support two further coherent directions: global commercial law and business, and law with sustainability. Their completed curricula differ pairwise by at least eleven courses. The separately evidenced Dutch-law direction is infeasible because UCR lacks the required Dutch-language doctrinal and procedural sequence. Production therefore reaches the maximum of three alternatives.
